subject: Enterprise activation: Nova Insurance — tenant isolation & activation milestones
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Huang <claire.huang@novains.com>, procure@novains.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Enterprise activation: Nova Insurance — tenant isolation & activation milestones

Hi team,

Quick context: Nova Insurance is on track to sign the Dedicated capacity commitment (NOVA-2026-345) but procurement and their security team have two gating asks that map to product work:

1) Tenant-level routing isolation — they need a routing policy so that requests from their tenant can be forced to a dedicated isolation path (eg. no shared cache/KV with other tenants, distinct egress IPs). They understand Dedicated helps but want a small product flag to enforce isolation for traffic routing.

2) Formal activation SLA — procurement needs an activation milestone and go-live readiness checklist (attestation they can hit production by a target date). They want us to commit to an activation window if the roadmap change is accepted.

Attachments: Nova_SLA_Request.pdf (procurement's required SLA template). I attached the high-level asks from their security questionnaire.

As the commercial owner, I need Product & Eng to confirm:
- Feasibility of the scoped "tenant routing isolation flag" as a minimal change (not full multi-tenant rewrite) — quick description of what work is required and major risks.
- Rough delivery timeline (best-case alpha + GA) if we prioritize this work now.
- Any required compensating controls (e.g., additional audits, temporary Dedicated-only limitation).

They've asked for a targeted activation date of 2026-10-29 (six weeks). If we can't commit to that, we need an explicit alternative (e.g., deliver an alpha + controls by that date and GA later).

I know this is short notice — asking for an initial feasibility note by EOD Thu (09/16) so I can update the customer and align procurement. If we can, please also indicate if this qualifies as a roadmap exception (i.e., ship earlier) and what trade-offs we'd take.

Thanks — Avery
--

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Enterprise activation: Nova Insurance — tenant isolation & activation milestones

Avery — thanks for the context. Quick clarifying questions before I map effort:

- Expected qps/peak concurrency for the tenant during ramp and steady state? (this drives whether we need dedicated routing or just config-level isolation)
- Which model families do they plan to run (open LLM vXX, quantized, or our recommended runtime)?
- Is the ask strictly at the networking/routing level, or do they also want logical data separation in cache/kv/embeddings?

Short thought: we can likely implement a scoped "tenant-routing-policy" flag that forces Dedicated traffic through an isolation path and disables cross-tenant KV sharing. The work touches routing policy evaluation (small), Dedicated config (medium), and docs + console (small). The largest unknown is egress IP controls (if they require predictable static IPs / VPC egress), which usually needs infra/networking changes and cloud partner coordination.

I'll draft a rough effort estimate once we have the QPS and model family. If procurement is rigid on 10/29 activation, we can prioritize a limited-scope alpha (routing flag + doc + verification steps) and defer full hardening (e.g., embedded cache eviction guarantees) to a later milestone.

– Dev

Dev Patel

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 13:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Enterprise activation: Nova Insurance — tenant isolation & activation milestones

Thanks, Avery + Dev. I spoke with infra and platform yesterday — here's a practical proposal and the trade-offs: 

Proposal (scoped):
- Implement a tenant-routing-policy flag (boolean) that: 1) tags requests from the tenant, 2) enforces Dedicated-only routing, and 3) disables prefix/KV sharing for that tenant. This is a config+policy layer change; it avoids a full multi-tenant rewrite.
- Provide a "Nova alpha" runbook and checklist we can sign off on by the activation date (networking tests, sample traffic burns, and verification steps).

Estimated effort:
- Routing policy + flag: ~2 engineer-weeks (Dev + 1) for core evaluation and enforcement code.
- Dedicated config + infra work: ~3 engineer-weeks (networking/infra) if egress IP control is required.
- Console + docs: 3-4 engineer-days.
- QA + validation runbook: 3-4 engineer-days.

Timeline: If we start immediately and prioritize (roadmap exception), we can produce an "alpha" with the routing flag, docs, and runbook by 2026-10-28. GA (full hardening including egress IPs and formal audit) would be later (TBD, depends on infra scheduling).

Risks/notes:
- Egress/static-IP/VPC egress may require cloud partner coordination and could add 2–4 weeks depending on region.
- This scoped change will not guarantee long-term eviction/hard isolation semantics for embedding stores; that would be a separate project. We should be explicit with Nova about the scope in the commitment.

Next steps I need from Sales/CS by EOD Fri (09/17):
- Confirm whether Nova accepts an Alpha-by-10/28 commitment (with GA later) or insists on GA-by-10/29.
- Provide expected peak QPS and a list of model families and any data residency/regulatory constraints.
- Legal/Security to sign off on the checklist (I can start the draft once we confirm scope).

Attaching: Prod_Roadmap_Summary.xlsx (internal roadmap snapshot).

If this looks actionable, I'll scope a short ticket and propose a three-sprint schedule (sprint 0: infra prep; sprint 1: routing policy; sprint 2: docs + QA).

– Marissa
--
Marissa Cole
Product Manager, Dedicated + Enterprise
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Thanks all — timeline and scope make sense. Quick summary and actions so nothing slips:

Decisions:
- Nova accepts Alpha-by-10/28 with GA TBD. They are okay with an alpha routing-flag + runbook as long as we are explicit about GA caveats.
- Use deal id NOVA-2026-345 in all internal tracking and when we draft the priority ask for Roadmap.

Action owners:
- Dev: prepare the routing-policy prototype + list of infra dependencies by 09/22. (Dev to include a short note on egress/static IP requirements)
- Marissa: create the Roadmap Exception request and schedule a 30-min triage review with Eng leads. Please attach Prod_Roadmap_Summary.xlsx and the proposed sprint plan. Target: 09/21.
- Karthik: loop in Security/Legal to review Nova_SLA_Request.pdf and start the checklist. Target: initial comments by 09/20.
- Me (Sales): I will coordinate procurement and confirm the alpha sign-off criteria with Claire this week.

Claire — thanks for being flexible on the GA date. We'll hold to the alpha target and flag any blocker ASAP. If Procurement needs specific language for the activation SLA, let me know and I'll get Legal involved.

Attachments: Nova_SLA_Request.pdf (from procurement).

If anyone foresees a blocker to the dates above, please call it out in this thread today so we can escalate. I'll start the internal prioritization ask once Marissa posts the Roadmap Exception doc.

Best,
